summary](.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/assets/context-report-summary/context-report-summary.html)\\n     2\\t\\n     3\\t---\\n     4\\t\\n     5\\t## A. Product Context\\n     6\\t\\n     7\\t1. **Current product state.** `decision-os` is a local browser canvas, a TypeScript backend ledger server, and workspace-local `.decision-os` data. The active repo workspace is dogfooding the product through `.decision-os/state.json`, which currently exposes `specs`, `data`, `performances`, and `tasks-system`.\\n     8\\t2. **Surface area.** The current surface includes route-addressed ledger tabs, a ledgers overview canvas, cards, zones, groups, relationships, canvas pan/zoom, selection, clipboard copy/paste, card resize, card Markdown, card fields, image carousels, HTML card assets, right-side threads, voice notes, transcription retry, live refresh, the `ledger-cli`, and the `generator-cli`.\\n     9\\t3. **Active workflows.** Operators inspect and edit ledgers on the canvas, create or move cards/zones/groups, review specs and performance evidence, paste images/files into threads, record voice notes, ask agents to treat unanswered notes, maintain card and zone summaries, and use report/mockup cards for PO analysis work.\\n    10\\t4. **Actors and roles.** The **operator** owns decisions, notes, approvals, and workspace intent. The **agent** reads threads, changes repo or ledger state, and replies in `# AGENT` sections. The **watcher** concept monitors unanswered notes. The **backend server** owns filesystem hydration and mutation. The **frontend runtime** owns transient interaction state. The **ledger CLI** is the maintenance and agent queue surface. The **OpenAI transcription provider** is optional and configured per workspace.\\n    11\\t5. **Adoption state.** Adoption evidence is internal and active: the repo workspace contains `289` spec cards, `40` data-model cards, `9` performance cards, and `27` task-system cards. No external customer analytics, production usage metrics, or support evidence were found in this research pass.\\n    12\\t6. **Active specs.** `specs.json` covers boot, navigation, canvas rendering, zones, selection, cards, threads, voice, refresh, groups, relationships, media, CLI tooling, generator tooling, and implementation architecture. `tasks-system.json` is the current Next Features surface and contains work around watcher loops, summary maintenance, task queues, report UX, and goal-object UX.\\n    13\\t7. **Known friction.** Threads currently carry too many responsibilities: conversation history, work queue, lock, status model, progress log, and recovery surface. Performance notes show drag and pan risk around browser frame production, layout-position writes, zone label reads, overlay rerenders, rich card surfaces, and relationship routing. Report UX notes show unresolved product boundaries for whether reports should be a card view, ledger type, goal cockpit tab, or embedded reader.\\n    14\\t\\n    15\\t---\\n    16\\t\\n    17\\t## B. Technical Context\\n    18\\t\\n    19\\t1. **Platform.** The backend is a Node/TypeScript HTTP server run through `tsx`; the frontend is a frameworkless TypeScript browser runtime served without a bundler; tests use Node's native test runner and Playwright-style browser specs; card syntax highlighting uses `highlight.js`.\\n    20\\t2. **Architecture.** The repo is split into `backend`, `frontend`, `ledger-cli`, `generator-cli`, `shared`, `tests`, `operations`, and workspace `.decision-os` files. The launcher `bin/decision-os-server.mjs` derives `DECISION_OS_FRONTEND_ROOT` and `TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH`, then starts `backend/src/server.ts` from the target workspace cwd.\\n    21\\t3. **Services and APIs.** The backend serves app routes `/`, `/ledgers`, and `/<ledgerId>`, state and ledger APIs under `/decision-os/state`, `/decision-os/<tab>`, `/decision-os/ledgers`, and `/decision-os/ledgers-canvas`, live refresh at `/api/ledger-content-events`, uploads at `/api/thread-image-upload`, `/api/thread-file-upload`, and `/api/voice-upload`, and transcription at `/api/transcribe` plus `/api/transcribe/retry`.\\n    22\\t4. **Data model.** `.decision-os/state.json` owns the ledger registry. Each ledger JSON owns `cards`, `annotations`, `relationships`, `viewport`, `threadFiles`, and related structured fields. Card bodies are durable Markdown files referenced by `comment.contentFile`. Thread histories are durable Markdown files under `.decision-os/threads/...`. Image layout persists through `imageSizes` in card JSON.\\n    23\\t5. **State ownership.** The filesystem is the canonical state store. The backend hydrates card Markdown and thread files into ledger responses, strips hydrated notes before writing, validates mutations, writes ledger JSON, writes card content files, and writes thread content files. The frontend owns transient state such as `activeTab`, `viewport`, `selection`, active tool, card tab state, open thread, draft text, scroll position, clipboard, and voice capture state.\\n    24\\t6. **Integrations.** Workspace settings in `.decision-os/.settings.json` can configure transcription with `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `openaiApiKey` and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`. The server also integrates with local filesystem watchers, local static asset serving, browser media capture, and the local CLI tools.\\n    25\\t7. **Permissions and security.** The default server host is `127.0.0.1`. Workspace asset serving is constrained to the active `.decision-os` root and allowed image, thread-file, or active-card asset paths. API keys and uploaded voice files are intended to stay local and uncommitted.\\n    26\\t8. **Observability.** The frontend and generator surfaces emit local telemetry facts. Performance evidence is stored in `operations/canvas-performance-study-2026-05-29.md` and `.decision-os/cards/performances/...`. Verification surfaces include `npm run typecheck:frontend`, `npm run typecheck:backend`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run test:front-back`, and live verification scripts under `tools/live-verify`.\\n    27\\t9. **Deployment.** Current deployment is local workspace execution, not hosted SaaS. Operator-facing sessions should run the detached launcher from the target workspace cwd, redirect logs under `/tmp`, and verify the HTTP route before reporting a URL.\\n    28\\t\\n    29\\t---\\n    30\\t\\n    31\\t## C. UX Context\\n    32\\t\\n    33\\t1. **Journeys.** A user opens a ledger route, reviews the canvas, selects or creates cards/zones/groups, edits geometry or content, opens the thread panel with `A`, writes or records notes, receives agent replies, reviews card media or report mockups, and can use CLI workflows for maintenance or agent treatment.\\n    34\\t2. **Screens and regions.** The main UX includes the tab registry, full-canvas ledger surface, toolbox, canvas controls, card detail layer, card overview layer, card description and fields tabs, relationship overlays, zone/group labels, deletion confirmation modals, right-side thread inspector, terminal-style composer, voice dock, telemetry/status copy, and the hidden ledgers overview.\\n    35\\t3. **States.** Important UI states include route mode, active ledger, viewport, zoom/detail mode, active tool, selection, grouped selection, clipboard, open card tab, low-detail versus hydrated card rendering, thread open/closed, draft restored, scroll restored, optimistic note pending, voice recording, transcription uploading, transcription failed, retry available, modal open, and external refresh received.\\n    36\\t4. **Entry points.** Primary entry points are `/`, `/ledgers`, `/<ledgerId>`, the tab registry, card/zone/group controls, the toolbox, keyboard shortcuts, thread buttons, thread upload/paste controls, voice controls, `ledger-cli`, and server launch commands.\\n    37\\t5. **Handoffs.** Operator notes hand off to agents through thread files. Agent replies hand back through `# AGENT` notes and durable card edits. Voice capture hands off from browser media capture to upload, transcription, optimistic note update, and retry. External filesystem edits hand off to the client through server-sent refresh events. Card Markdown hands off to backend hydration and frontend Markdown/media rendering.\\n    38\\t6. **Information architecture.** The current workspace separates **Specs** for behavior contracts, **Data** for base classes and relationships, **Performances** for measured canvas performance evidence, and **Tasks System** for Next Features. At the object level, cards, zones, groups, relationships, and threads are the main navigable units.\\n    39\\t7. **Accessibility.** The implemented keyboard contract includes `A`, `X`, `Esc`, `Del`, `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+V`, and `Ctrl+D`. Deletion confirmations support keyboard handling. Some rendered controls expose labels or titles. Full WCAG coverage, screen-reader behavior, focus order, and color-contrast audits were not verified in this pass.\\n    40\\t8. **Copy and language.** Agent replies must be English. Thread copy uses `# OPERATOR` and `# AGENT` sections. Durable card content should stay concrete, implementation-ready, and traceable to source files or ledgers. The in-app Keys panel should remain the operator-facing keyboard contract.\\n    41\\t9. **Interaction constraints.** Expensive card detail is hydrated only when detail is visible. Pan/zoom and drag must preserve responsive frame production. Delete actions require confirmation. Thread and voice tooling must not steal editing keystrokes. Media dimensions must persist independent of canvas zoom. HTML embeds must stay under allowed card asset paths.\\n    42\\t\\n    43\\t---\\n    44\\t\\n    45\\t## D. Context Boundaries\\n    46\\t\\n    47\\t1. **In scope.** This context covers the current `decision-os` repo, the active repo-local `.decision-os` workspace, existing code, existing docs, active ledgers, task cards, performance notes, thread model, CLI model, and local runtime behavior visible from source inspection.\\n    48\\t2. **Out of scope.** This context does not cover a hosted deployment, multi-tenant permissions, billing, external customer research, market positioning, production analytics, support tickets, or non-repo workspaces.\\n    49\\t3. **Unverified areas.** This pass did not start a browser session, run automated tests, inspect live decision-os workspace state, validate a real transcription API key, measure current browser performance, audit accessibility with assistive technology, or confirm external operator adoption beyond repo evidence.\\n    50\\t4. **Source gaps.** There is no discovered analytics baseline, customer interview set, support ticket sample, hosted deployment runbook, centralized telemetry sink, or current CI result attached to this note. Some README examples still describe older `tabs` wording while current state uses a `ledgers` registry.\\n    51\\t5. **Cross-team dependencies.** The only confirmed dependency outside the local repo is optional OpenAI transcription configuration. Product-boundary decisions for reports, work queues, watcher agents, and goal objects remain operator-owned unless a future card assigns explicit ownership.\\n    52\\t6. **Evidence sources.** Primary evidence came from `README.md`, `.decision-os/state.json`, `.decision-os/specs.json`, `.decision-os/data.json`, `.decision-os/performances.json`, `.decision-os/tasks-system.json`, `backend/src/business/server/helper/create-http-server.ts`, `backend/src/business/ledger/helper/apply-ledger-mutation.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/boot/controller/boot-surface.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/render-ledger-surface.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/input/controller/handle-keyboard.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/thread/effect/render-thread-panel.ts`, `.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/card-agent-autonomy-work-queue.md`, `.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/card-2395850a-c528-4689-a138-73a30b684602.md`, and `.decision-os/cards/performances/...`.\\n\",\"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough\":{\"turn_id\":\"019f3d81-f556-7433-9b32-66a812c294b5\"}}}\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-skill-task-list.md:5928:/home/jbb/.codex/sessions/2026/07/09/rollout-2026-07-09T12-44-43-019f4568-2f76-7bb0-93c2-fbbbed5c62b6.jsonl:86:{\"timestamp\":\"2026-07-09T05:46:44.863Z\",\"type\":\"response_item\",\"payload\":{\"type\":\"function_call_output\",\"call_id\":\"call_GIXrjkLCEv7YjfBBzR0z286e\",\"output\":\"Chunk ID: 778d62\\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\\nProcess exited with code 0\\nOriginal token count: 1892\\nOutput:\\n---\\nname: executor-spec\\ndescription: Transform Specs, Data Model, Runtime State and executor-stack analysis output into a master ledger then used to create the scaffold of the whole codebase or codebase section. Read the WHOLE document, not only a subsection. CREATE the master-ledger document FIRST, then WRITE each section one AFTER the other.\\n---\\n\\n# Executor Spec\\n\\n## A. Formatting Contract\\n\\n1. **Headings:** use `H2` card sections with uppercase letters: `## A. Scope`, `## B. Contract`, `## C. Acceptance Criteria`.\\n2. **Dividers:** put `---` between card sections.\\n3. **Lists:** write section content as numbered list items: `1.`, `2.`, `3.`.\\n4. **Bold:** use **bold** for the important words that carry the point.\\n5. **Backticks:** use `backticks` for technical, secondary, exact, or literal terms: file paths, routes, config keys, commands, IDs, statuses, branch names, code symbols, and literal values.\\n\\nThe purpose is to turn `stack analysis` into a `Master Ledger`, containing the complete or partial scaffold, depending on the `operator` demand. \\n\\n---\\n\\n## A. Nomenclature and Definitions\\n\\n### A.1 Spec\\n\\n- A `spec` is an `operator`-authored truth constraint over the system: it defines an expected property, behavior, capability, or invariant that must hold in *all applicable situations*, **independent of how the system is implemented**.\\n\\n- An `Anti-Spec` is an operator-authored truth constraint that says what the system must not do, must reject, or must never infer.\\n\\n### A.2 Data Model\\n\\nA `Data Model` is the `operator`-authored schema of the system’s *durable and contractual data*: the entities, tables, records, fields, identities, relationships, and constraints that the implementation must *store, load, validate, and exchange*.\\n\\n### A.3 Runtime State\\n`Runtime State` is the current *in-memory state* of the running system: the session, UI, interaction, process, cache, selection, pending operation, telemetry, and *transient values* that can change *while the system executes* and that may be derived from, synchronized with, or eventually persisted into the `Data Model`.\\n\\n### A.4 Root Block\\n\\n- A Root Block is a top-level system part with its own runtime or ownership boundary.  \\n\\n- It can be a frontend, backend, mobile app, CLI, worker, engine, library, QA harness, or shared contract package when it owns its own project shape.  \\n\\n- Root blocks should have already been defined by the previous `executor-stack` step.\\n\\n- A root block is a package/app/engine/tool with its own source, package, build process, metadata, README/AGENTS guidance, runtime entrypoint, data, generated and tests.\\n\\n\\n### A.5 Domain\\n\\nA `domain` is a business subject area inside a `Root Block`.\\n\\nIt groups the logic that owns the same business object, capability, or invariant.\\n\\n```text\\nbusiness/\\n  auth/\\n  billing/\\n  podcast/\\n  subscription/\\n  account/\\n```\\n\\nA `domain` is not a screen and not a route.\\n\\n- `route/auth.route.ext` receives auth-related input.\\n- `ui/component/login/` renders a login screen.\\n- `business/auth/` owns auth behavior: login, logout, register, recover password, permissions.\\n\\nInside a `domain`, use the Skill behavior nouns:\\n\\n```text\\nbusiness/\\n  auth/\\n    action/\\n    controller/\\n    helper/\\n    effect/\\n```\\n\\nShort definition:\\n\\n> A `domain` is the business ownership boundary for related `actions`, `controllers`, `helpers`, and `effects` inside a `Root Block`.\\n\\n###### Domain and Data Model\\n\\nA `domain` can match a `Data Model` entity, but it does not have to.\\n\\n- A `Data Model` is durable and contractual data: tables, records, fields, relationships, schemas.\\n- A `domain` is business ownership: the area that owns behavior, invariants, controllers, helpers, and effects.\\n\\nThey often overlap:\\n\\n```text\\nData Model: User\\nDomain: auth or account\\n\\nData Model: Subscription\\nDomain: subscription or billing\\n\\nData Model: Podcast\\nDomain: podcast\\n```\\n\\nThey can also diverge:\\n\\n```text\\nDomain: checkout\\nData Models: cart, user, subscription, payment, invoice\\n\\nDomain: auth\\nData Models: user, session, permission, token\\n\\nDomain: search\\nData Models: podcast, tag, author\\n```\\n\\nRule:\\n\\n> A `domain` is derived from business behavior and invariants, not mechanically from table names or model names.\\n\\nIf one `Data Model` owns a coherent lifecycle, it may become one `domain`. If a lifecycle crosses several `Data Models`, the `domain` should follow the lifecycle, not the storage shape.\\n\\n\\n\\n### A.6 Screen || Page\\n\\nA `screen` or `page` is a user-facing UI surface inside a frontend, client, or mobile `Root Block`.\\n\\nIt is the presentation composition that the operator can see or interact with.\\n\\nA `screen` or `page` can:\\n\\n- render `components`\\n- read `Runtime State`\\n- emit `inputs`\\n- display `effects` feedback\\n\\nA `screen` or `page` is not a `domain`.\\n\\nA `screen` or `page` can involve several `domains` at the same time.\\n\\nExample:\\n\\n```text\\nui/\\n   component/\\n      login/\\n      checkout/\\n      account-settings/\\n   style/\\n      login/\\n      checkout/\\n      account-settings/\\n```\\n\\n*checkout* as a screen may involve:\\n\\n```text\\nbusiness/\\n  cart/\\n  account/\\n  subscription/\\n  payment/\\n```\\n\\nA `screen` or `page` is also not a *route*.\\n\\n- A *route* receives navigation or browser input.\\n- A `screen` or `page` renders the UI surface.\\n- A `controller` owns behavior after an `action` is created.\\n- A `domain` owns business logic and invariants.\\n\\nRule:\\n\\n> A `screen` or `page` is a UI composition boundary, not a business ownership boundary.\\n\\n### A.7 Component\\n\\nA `component` is a UI building block.  \\n\\nIt renders part of a `screen` or `page`.  \\n\\nA `component` can receive data, display state, and emit user inputs like clicks, typing, or gestures.  \\n\\nA `component` does not own business logic. Business logic belongs to `controllers` inside `business/{domain}`.  \\n\\n\\n\\n\\n### A.8 Test\\nProves the full flow through `input`, `action`, `controller`, `helper`, and `effect` with the `help` of `telemetry`\\n\\n### A.9 Input\\nA named entry condition *from outside* the behavior. It is part of the `spec` surface, not an execution unit.  \\n> Examples: browser load, click, pointer drag, HTTP request, file watcher event, server refresh event.\\n\\n### A.10 Action\\nCommand **payload** describing what happened or what is requested.\\n\\n### A.11 Controller\\nBehavior owner. It branches, orchestrates, and decides the path.  \\nIt **DOES NOT** contains implementation details, only branching, functions calls: `helpers`, `effects` and `telemetry`\\n\\n### A.12 Helper\\n*Implementation extraction* from `controller` logic.  \\nIt may be sync or async and may do IO.\\n\\n> Exemple: parsing text, validating data, querying a database, writing a file, deriving a branch decision, formatting output, calculating geometry, normalizing values or loading configuration.\\n\\n### A.13 Effect\\nFinal output call; called by the `controller` with no expected response.  \\nA `controller` can call several `effects` along the execution. \\n\\n> Exemple: Effects are final output calls used by controllers for things like publishing a state change, emitting a UI update, sending a response, notifying another system, committing a visible write result, or reporting telemetry.\\n\\n### A.14 Telemetry\\n\\n`Telemetry` is the execution evidence emitted during the flow so `tests`, `operators`, and `stack trace` can prove what happened.\\n\\nIt records things like the selected `controller branch`, `helper` calls, `effect` calls, `arguments`, `timing`, `errors`.  \\n\\n`Telemetry` is *observational*: it may report execution, but it **MUST NOT** decide behavior, replace controller branching, or become the source of truth for the result.\\n\",\"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough\":{\"turn_id\":\"019f4568-3024-76b3-82dd-294e499393b6\"}}}\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-skill-task-list.md:5946:/home/jbb/.codex/sessions/2026/07/09/rollout-2026-07-09T12-45-36-019f4568-fdc0-7b70-8d43-b83b7d790b0a.jsonl:166:{\"timestamp\":\"2026-07-09T05:49:50.921Z\",\"type\":\"response_item\",\"payload\":{\"type\":\"function_call_output\",\"call_id\":\"call_jo9Q8nWlk5RCuZXMuUbVfNif\",\"output\":\"Chunk Summary](.decision-os/cards/tasks-system/assets/goal-linked-specs-summary/summary.html)\n\n## A. Source Boundary\n\n1. **Allowed source set.** This card uses the `Decision OS Context`, `PO Goal Analysis Format`, and `Goal Object UX` cards, the operator thread on this card, source files, tests, and `README.md`. It does not use `.decision-os/specs.json` or any spec-ledger card body as a source for linked specs.\n2. **Spec-id rule.** A `spec id` is preserved only when the id appears in code or test evidence, for example `frontend/index.html` `data-spec` attributes or executable test headers. If the codebase shows behavior but no durable id, the `spec id` is recorded as `unknown`.\n3. **Base goal.** Create an interface inside Decision OS that lets a human operator read and inspect PO goal-analysis report results for the current goal. The current goal is recursive: build the process and interface for seeing how a goal fits into the existing product.\n4. **Context report fact.** Decision OS is a local browser canvas, TypeScript backend ledger server, and workspace-local `.decision-os` state. The current Next Features surface is `tasks-system`, shown as `Tasks System` in `.decision-os/state.json` and as `Ledger: Next Features` in `.decision-os/ledgers-canvas.json`.\n5. **Goal-object fact.** The existing `Goal Object UX` card defines `Goal`, `Reports`, `Specs`, and `Tasks` as separate objects, and its global goal cockpit direction exposes `Specs`, `Reports`, and `Tasks` as tabs.\n\n---\n\n## B. Goal Spec Link\n\n1. **Goal need.** The operator needs a readable goal-analysis interface that shows how the active goal relates to product context, technical context, UX context, linked specs, missing specs, and gaps.\n2. **Affected product area.** The affected surface is the Decision OS ledger canvas, especially the `tasks-system` Next Features ledger, card Markdown rendering, thread inspector, report-card assets, and potential goal-cockpit navigation.\n3. **Affected workflow.** The workflow is: operator creates or states a goal, agent/context report extracts facts, Decision OS presents linked specs and reports, operator inspects rows or opens threads, and later work can derive tasks or report ledgers from that factual state.\n4. **Affected actor or role.** The primary actor is the **operator**. Supporting roles are the **agent** that extracts and writes durable state, the **frontend runtime** that renders the interface, and the **backend server** that hydrates and persists ledger files.\n5. **Relevant context fact.** The context card states that report UX boundaries are unresolved: reports could be a card view, ledger type, goal cockpit tab, or embedded reader. The codebase already supports route-addressed ledgers, Markdown cards, image carousels, HTML embeds, threads, and voice notes.\n6. **Current behavior.** Report facts can be stored in card Markdown, report mockups can be shown through adjacent images or active-ledger HTML embeds, threads attach operator feedback to cards, and ledgers load through `/decision-os/state` and `/decision-os/<tab>`.\n7. **Expected behavior.** The goal-linked spec surface should show the base goal, goal/spec link fields, linked specs with source and relevance, missing specs, and gaps. It should remain facts-only: no recommendation, selected path, approval gate, or implementation plan.\n8. **Acceptance signal.** The `Goal Linked Specs` card contains source-traceable entries for `goal need`, `affected product area`, `affected workflow`, `actor`, `context fact`, `current behavior`, `expected behavior`, `acceptance signal`, linked specs, missing specs, and spec gaps, with no direct spec-ledger extraction.\n\n---\n\n## C. Linked Specs\n\n1. **`e6a91d34` - decision-os state drives ledger tabs and routes.** **Source:** `frontend/index.html`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/load-decision-os-state.ts`, and `tests/browser/navigation/decision-os-state-drives-ledger-tabs-and-routes.spec.ts`. **Relation:** `support`. **Goal relevance:** a goal-analysis interface must be reachable from the active ledger registry, and `tasks-system` is the current Next Features ledger.\n2. **`f2d6c8b1` - Tab click loads the active ledger graph into the canvas.** **Source:** `frontend/index.html`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/load-active-ledger-state.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/render-ledger-surface.ts`, and `tests/browser/navigation/tab-click-loads-the-active-ledger-graph-into-the-canvas.spec.ts`. **Relation:** `support`. **Goal relevance:** report, spec, and task surfaces must render as active ledger graph state, not detached static pages.\n3. **`cd58fd49` - card descriptions are parsed and rendered as markdown.** **Source:** `tests/browser/card/card-descriptions-are-parsed-and-rendered-as-markdown.spec.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/helper/parse-ledger-card-markdown.ts`, and `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/component/render-ledger-card-markdown.ts`. **Relation:** `support`. **Goal relevance:** the current report and spec-link inventory can live in a durable Markdown card without a schema change.\n4. **`unknown` - refresh preserves canvas continuity during operator work.** **Source:** `tests/browser/refresh/the-refresh-system-preserves-canvas-continuity-during-operator-work.spec.ts`, `backend/src/business/server/helper/create-http-server.ts`, and `frontend/src/runtime/refresh/*`. **Relation:** `constrain`. **Goal relevance:** agent edits to report/spec-link cards should not disrupt the operator's current canvas or thread context.\n10. **`c4e8b91a` - Cards indicate when the latest thread answer is from the agent.** **Source:** `tests/browser/card/cards-indicate-when-the-latest-thread-answer-is-from-the-agent.spec.ts` and `frontend/src/runtime/card/helper/card-has-agent-last-answer.ts`. **Relation:** `support`. **Goal relevance:** treated goal-analysis notes need visible feedback that the latest unanswered operator request was answered.\n11. **`c5a84d77` - Specs and data ledgers are available from decision-os `.decision-os`.** **Source:** `tests/browser/refresh/specs-and-data-ledgers-are-available-from-decision-os.spec.ts`. **Relation:** `non-goal` for this card. **Goal relevance:** the product can serve the spec ledger, but the operator explicitly excluded any spec ledger as an extraction source for this research pass.\n\n---\n\n## D. Missing Specs\n\n1. **Goal object data spec.** **Implied requirement:** a goal needs durable identity, current statement, linked surfaces, and generated objects. **Missing acceptance signal:** no code-defined `Goal` object type or route was found. **Missing data spec:** `shared/schemas/core-types.ts` has `Card`, `Thread`, and `CanvasLedger`, but no `Goal`.\n2. **Goal/spec link schema.** **Implied requirement:** persist `goal need`, `affected product area`, `workflow`, `actor`, `context fact`, `current behavior`, `expected behavior`, and `acceptance signal`. **Missing technical spec:** no `SpecLink` schema, mutation action, or renderer was found in source.\n3. **Spec row review UX.** **Implied requirement:** each goal-linked spec row can expose approve, rephrase, reject, and thread actions. **Missing UX spec:** the code supports generic threads and voice, but no spec-row component, row-level thread target, or row review state exists.\n4. **Report container boundary.** **Implied requirement:** report results need a durable readable surface. **Missing product-boundary spec:** the source evidence does not settle whether reports are cards, ledgers, goal-cockpit tabs, embedded readers, or a combination.\n5. **Report ledger navigation.** **Implied requirement:** report cards can open report ledgers and zooming out can return to the global goal view. **Missing technical spec:** current code has ledgers-canvas zoom behavior and route state, but no report-ledger return contract tied to a goal object.\n6. **Task flow representation.** **Implied requirement:** tasks can be list-first, grouped into flows, and optionally opened as a graph. **Missing data spec:** no task-flow object, system-prompt link, or formatted-output object was found in the current shared schema.\n7. **Source policy enforcement.** **Implied requirement:** some research passes must extract specs only from a context card and codebase, not from a spec ledger. **Missing operational spec:** no CLI or runtime source-filter contract was found for enforcing this policy.\n8. **Measurement and validation.** **Implied requirement:** acceptance for \"visualize correctly\" needs evidence. **Missing acceptance signal:** no analytics, usability observation, screen-reader audit, or live browser verification is attached to this card.\n\n---\n\n## E. Spec Gaps\n\n1. **Contradiction.** Durable card formatting prefers numbered lists, but `parse-ledger-card-markdown.ts` only parses unordered `-` or `*` list syntax as a list block. Numbered lines render as paragraphs in the current card Markdown renderer.\n2. **Unknown.** The codebase does not show a first-class `Goal`, `Report`, `SpecLink`, or `TaskFlow` object in `shared/schemas/core-types.ts`; this may be intentionally pending because the object model is still being designed.\n3. **Unverified fact.** The context card states workspace counts and active adoption evidence, but this card did not run a live browser session or analytics check. Treat those counts as context-card evidence, not external usage proof.\n4. **Source gap.** `frontend/index.html` contains many `data-spec` ids without titles; executable tests provide titles for many but not all ids. Rows above use test titles where available and mark unsupported titles as `unknown`.\n5. **Ownership gap.** The context card says product-boundary decisions for reports, work queues, watcher agents, and goal objects remain operator-owned unless a future card assigns explicit ownership.\n6. **Product-boundary decision.** The report surface is still unresolved between card view, ledger type, goal cockpit tab, and embedded reader. The current code supports all adjacent primitives but does not choose one.\n7. **Technical constraint.** HTML embeds must live under `.decision-os/cards/<active-ledger>/assets/` and end in `.html`; `render-ledger-card-html-embeds.ts` rejects other locations.\n8. **UX constraint.** Card detail rendering is expensive and hydrated only for visible cards. A long goal-analysis report must remain usable when the canvas is in low-detail or overview mode.\n9. **Data constraint.** Current thread target kinds are `card`, `zone`, `group`, and `canvas`; there is no confirmed section-level or spec-row-level thread target.\n10. **Dependency constraint.** Voice rephrase behavior depends on browser capture and optional OpenAI transcription configuration; the context card marks transcription as workspace-local and optional.\n\n---\n\n## F. Scope\n\n1. **Operator request.** Analyze the refresh and interaction issue tied to this card, reformat the durable card markdown, and add the commit history for the fixes that were expected to repair the problem.\n2. **Target behavior.** During card drag, group drag, zone drag, resize, pan, wheel zoom, thread edits, and Codex content refresh, Decision OS must keep the current canvas interaction attached to the same ledger, same pointer session, same selected objects, same viewport, and same locally moved geometry.\n3. **Primary failure class.** The existing fixes protect server refresh merge results for geometry and viewport values, but they do not protect the active interaction session that connects `state.pointer.targetId`, `state.selection`, `state.viewport`, rendered DOM nodes, and `patch-geometry` payloads.\n4. **In-scope runtime paths.** The affected files are `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/load-active-ledger-state.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/refresh/controller/refresh-runtime-state.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/refresh/effect/subscribe-ledger-content-events.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/gesture/controller/handle-pointer-down.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/gesture/controller/handle-pointer-move.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/gesture/controller/handle-pointer-up.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/selection/effect/move-selected.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/commit-selected-ledger-geometry.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/helper/active-ledger-geometry.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/card/effect/resize-selected-card.ts`, and `frontend/src/runtime/zone/effect/resize-selected-zone.ts`.\n\n---\n\n## B. Verified Current Behavior\n\n1. **Ledger load clears selection.** `loadActiveLedgerState()` fetches the active ledger, merges local canvas geometry through `mergeLocalCanvasStateIntoLedger()`, restores the current viewport for the same `activeLedgerId`, and then resets `state.selection` to empty.\n2. **Manual refresh clears selection twice.** `refreshRuntimeState()` preserves the local viewport for the next ledger id, reads persisted state, clears `state.selection`, hydrates persisted geometry, then calls `loadActiveLedgerState()`, which clears `state.selection` again.\n3. **Ledger content refresh remounts canvas state.** `reloadLedgerContent()` calls `loadActiveLedgerState()`, calls `renderCanvasSurface()`, and optionally resizes the changed card with `resizeChangedCardToContent()`. It does not capture the active pointer session and does not preserve current selection explicitly.\n4. **Thread content refresh can restore stale selection.** `reloadThreadContent()` captures `const selection = state.selection`, awaits `loadActiveLedgerState()`, then assigns `state.selection = selection`. If the operator changes selection while the fetch is in flight, the old snapshot can overwrite the newer selection.\n5. **Pointer down stores target identity.** `handlePointerDown()` records `targetKind` and `targetId` in `state.pointer`, then calls `selectTarget()` for drag and resize paths when selection needs to change.\n6. **Pointer move uses live selection.** `handlePointerMove()` calls `moveSelected(canvasDx, canvasDy)` for drag and group gestures. `moveSelected()` reads `state.selection.cardIds`, `state.selection.zoneIds`, and `state.selection.groupIds` at movement time.\n7. **Pointer up commits live selection.** `handlePointerUp()` calls `commitSelectedLedgerGeometry()` for drag, group, and resize releases. `commitSelectedLedgerGeometry()` calls `selectedLedgerGeometryPayload()` with its default `state.selection`.\n8. **Wheel zoom mutates viewport directly.** `handleWheel()` updates `state.viewport`, calls `scheduleViewportPersistence()`, and calls `scheduleViewportTransform()`. Commit `e1a55b5` protects in-flight `loadActiveLedgerState()` from overwriting current viewport values, but current tests do not exercise a real wheel event racing with ledger content refresh and delayed viewport persistence.\n\n---\n\n## C. Repair Commit History\n\n1. **`bed5d24` - Preserve local canvas state during ledger refresh.** This commit added `mergeLocalCanvasStateIntoLedger()`, added `state.activeLedgerId`, preserved local card, zone, and group geometry by id during same-ledger refresh, and preserved the current viewport during same-ledger refresh. Its tests cover same-ledger geometry plus viewport preservation and non-geometry mutation responses. It did not protect `state.selection`, active pointer identity, active drag target identity, active pan session state, and refreshes that complete after the viewport changes while fetch is in flight.\n2. **`e7ff7ff` - Preserve local geometry on geometry patches.** This commit added `localCanvasMergeOptionsForMutation()` so `patch-geometry` responses accept the server geometry for the geometry just committed while preserving unrelated newer local geometry. Its tests cover unrelated card, zone, and group geometry during `patch-geometry`. It did not bind the geometry payload to the pointer session that started the drag, so a stale live `state.selection` can still produce the wrong payload.\n3. **`e1a55b5` - Keep current viewport during ledger refresh.** This commit moved the same-ledger viewport snapshot in `loadActiveLedgerState()` to after the fetch and JSON parse, then added a test where `state.viewport.x`, `state.viewport.y`, and `state.viewport.scale` change while the server load is in flight. It covers viewport values during `loadActiveLedgerState()`. It does not cover active pointer pan continuity, wheel persistence timer freshness, selection continuity, and drag identity continuity.\n4. **`88856a3` - Preserve multi-selection on drag start.** This adjacent commit protects the initial drag selection rules through `selectionIncludesTarget()`. It does not protect the selection after refresh code mutates `state.selection`.\n5. **`474ab51` - Prevent card focus from committing geometry.** This adjacent commit keeps click focus away from geometry commit paths through click-movement checks. It does not address refresh races after a real drag starts.\n6. **`ed9757f` - Freeze drag geometry on pointer release.** This adjacent commit clears the pointer before a slow geometry commit can accept later cursor movement and adds `frontend/test/runtime/drag-release-freeze.integration.test.ts`. It does not protect the target selection used before pointer release.\n7. **`93a2aa7` - Fix geometry commit thread render stall.** This adjacent commit reduces thread rendering during geometry commits and keeps pan release from forcing full canvas render. It does not protect active gesture state from ledger refresh.\n\n---\n\n## D. Remaining Defect\n\n1. **Selection rollback.** `loadActiveLedgerState()` and `refreshRuntimeState()` still clear `state.selection`. `reloadThreadContent()` still restores a pre-refresh selection snapshot after an async ledger load. The result can be empty selection, older selection, and newer operator selection being overwritten.\n2. **Wrong drag target.** `handlePointerDown()` records the intended target in `state.pointer.targetId`, but drag movement and geometry commit use live `state.selection`. A refresh between pointer down and pointer move can make `moveSelected()` move the wrong card, zone, group, and attached selection set.\n3. **Wrong geometry payload.** A refresh between pointer move and pointer up can make `commitSelectedLedgerGeometry()` commit geometry for the current `state.selection`, not the selected ids that belonged to the pointer session.\n4. **Detached resize target.** `resizeSelectedCard()` and `resizeSelectedZone()` rely on `state.pointer.target` as a DOM element. A content refresh can remount the canvas while a pointer session is active, leaving the saved element stale even though `state.pointer.targetId` still identifies the intended ledger record.\n5. **Pan session gap.** Viewport values are preserved, but no test proves that an active pan session keeps `state.pointer`, continues applying deltas, and finishes cleanly after `loadActiveLedgerState()`, `requestLedgerContentRefresh()`, and `refreshRuntimeState()`.\n6. **Wheel refresh gap.** Scale preservation is tested as a direct state mutation, but a real wheel event with `scheduleViewportPersistence()` and `scheduleViewportTransform()` is not tested against a simultaneous ledger refresh.\n7. **Coverage gap.** The browser refresh spec `tests/browser/refresh/the-refresh-system-preserves-canvas-continuity-during-operator-work.spec.ts` delegates to `assertFrontendSpec()` and checks source tokens. It is not an interaction race reproduction.\n\n---\n\n## E. Root Cause\n\n1. **Shared mutable selection.** `state.selection` is both the durable visible selection and the live operand for active drag, group drag, and resize. Refresh code also mutates the same object, so refresh owns a value that pointer code assumes is stable.\n2. **Async refresh writes global state after awaits.** `loadActiveLedgerState()`, `reloadLedgerContent()`, `reloadThreadContent()`, and `refreshRuntimeState()` write selection and active ledger state after network and file-refresh awaits without checking whether a pointer session started, moved, changed selection, and reached release during the wait.\n3. **Pointer session lacks a geometry selection snapshot.** `state.pointer` stores `targetKind` and `targetId`, but not the full selected card, zone, and group id set that should receive movement deltas and release commits.\n4. **DOM target is treated as stable.** Resize helpers use the saved DOM element instead of resolving the target by `targetId` against the current render and active ledger record.\n\n---\n\n## F. Selected Fix Contract\n\n1. **Capture a pointer selection snapshot.** After `handlePointerDown()` finishes `selectTarget()` for `drag`, `group`, and `resize`, store `state.pointer.selectionSnapshot` with `cardIds`, `zoneIds`, `groupIds`, `targetKind`, `targetId`, and the current `ledgerStateId`.\n2. **Move explicit gesture selection.** Update `moveSelected()` to accept an explicit selection argument and use that selection for ledger geometry mutation, DOM position patches, telemetry, zone labels, relationship overlays, and canvas controls. `handlePointerMove()` must pass `state.pointer.selectionSnapshot` for active drag and group gestures.\n3. **Commit explicit gesture selection.** Update `commitSelectedLedgerGeometry()` to accept an explicit selection argument and pass that selection to `selectedLedgerGeometryPayload(selection)`. `handlePointerUp()` must commit `pointerSession.selectionSnapshot` for drag, group, and resize releases.\n4. **Resolve resize targets by id.** Update `resizeSelectedCard()` and `resizeSelectedZone()` so they resolve the active DOM node from `state.pointer.targetId` when the saved `state.pointer.target` is missing, detached, and stale. Ledger geometry must be patched through `activeLedgerCardMap()` and `activeLedgerAnnotationMap()` by id.\n5. **Preserve same-ledger selection through refresh.** Update `loadActiveLedgerState()` so same-ledger refresh keeps the current selection after pruning selected ids that no longer exist in the refreshed ledger. Route changes and ledger changes remain the only paths that clear selection.\n6. **Protect active pointer selection during refresh.** When `state.pointer` is active, refresh code must keep `state.pointer.selectionSnapshot` unchanged and must restore visible `state.selection` from that snapshot after the active ledger merge finishes.\n7. **Prevent stale thread refresh selection restore.** Update `reloadThreadContent()` so it restores the captured selection only when no pointer session is active and the visible selection has not changed since the snapshot was captured. If selection changed during the await, the newer selection remains authoritative.\n8. **Keep viewport preservation unchanged.** Keep the `e1a55b5` behavior that samples `state.viewport` after the fetch and JSON parse in `loadActiveLedgerState()`. Add race tests for wheel and pan paths instead of replacing this behavior.\n\n---\n\n## G. Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. **Active drag plus ledger load.** With `pointerdown` on `card-a`, a same-ledger `loadActiveLedgerState()` completing before `pointermove` must not move `card-b`, must not commit `card-b`, and must commit only `card-a`.\n2. **Multi-selection drag plus content refresh.** With `card-a`, `zone-a`, and `group-a` selected at pointer down, `requestLedgerContentRefresh()` completing before pointer up must preserve the same movement target set and must commit geometry for that exact set.\n3. **Resize plus remount.** With a resize session active, a render from `reloadLedgerContent()` must not detach the resize operation from the intended card, zone, and group id. The final geometry payload must use `state.pointer.targetId`.\n4. **Thread refresh selection freshness.** If `reloadThreadContent()` starts with `card-a` selected and the operator selects `card-b` before the load resolves, the final visible selection must stay on `card-b`.\n5. **Same-ledger selection preservation.** A same-ledger load must preserve existing selected ids that still exist in the refreshed ledger and must remove selected ids missing from the refreshed ledger.\n6. **Manual refresh during pan.** During a pointer pan session, `refreshRuntimeState()` must keep `state.pointer.intent` as `pan`, preserve the latest `state.viewport`, allow the next pointer move to continue from the current pointer coordinates, and allow pointer up to call `finishPointer()`.\n7. **Wheel zoom race.** A wheel zoom followed by same-ledger refresh must leave the latest `state.viewport.x`, `state.viewport.y`, and `state.viewport.scale` in memory and in the next `scheduleViewportPersistence()` write.\n8. **Browser spec strength.** The refresh browser test must include an interaction-race assertion instead of relying only on source-token evidence from `assertFrontendSpec()`.\n\n---\n\n## H. Test Plan\n\n1. **Runtime drag race tests.** Add tests to `frontend/test/runtime/active-ledger-zone-lifecycle.integration.test.ts` and `frontend/test/runtime/drag-release-freeze.integration.test.ts` for drag, multi-selection drag, and resize across `loadActiveLedgerState()` and `requestLedgerContentRefresh()`.\n2. **Thread refresh race test.** Extend `frontend/test/runtime/ledger-content-refresh.integration.test.ts` with an async `requestThreadContentRefresh()` case that changes selection before the load resolves and verifies the newer selection wins.\n3. **Pan and wheel race tests.** Extend `frontend/test/runtime/canvas-pan-performance.integration.test.ts` with active pan refresh continuity, and add a wheel refresh case that runs `handleWheel()`, completes a same-ledger load, and verifies current viewport plus scheduled persistence state.\n4. **Browser refresh proof.** Replace the thin `tests/browser/refresh/the-refresh-system-preserves-canvas-continuity-during-operator-work.spec.ts` source-token assertion with a Playwright interaction that starts drag, triggers refresh, moves, releases, and checks the final geometry target.\n5. **Focused command.** Run `cd frontend && node --test --import tsx test/runtime/active-ledger-zone-lifecycle.integration.test.ts test/runtime/ledger-content-refresh.integration.test.ts test/runtime/canvas-pan-performance.integration.test.ts test/runtime/drag-release-freeze.integration.test.ts`.\n6. **Browser command.** Run `node --test --import ./frontend/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs tests/browser/refresh/the-refresh-system-preserves-canvas-continuity-during-operator-work.spec.ts`.\n7. **Typecheck command.** Run `npm run typecheck:frontend`.\n\n---\n\n## I. Result\n\n1. **Treated.** I rewrote the card into a complete implementation-ready spec for the refresh and active-interaction continuity bug.\n2. **Durable edit.** The updated card is `.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md`.\n3. **Run summary.** I updated `.decision-os/runs/codex-skills/bugs/codex-skill-1783610702748-b1123a49.md` with a concise inspection summary.\n\n---\n\n## B. Key Finding\n\n1. **Root cause.** Current fixes preserve merged ledger geometry and viewport values, but the active gesture still depends on live `state.selection`. Refresh code can clear selection and thread refresh can restore stale selection while a pointer session is active.\n2. **Risk.** A refresh between `pointerdown`, `pointermove`, and `pointerup` can make `moveSelected()` and `commitSelectedLedgerGeometry()` move and commit the wrong card, zone, and group set.\n3. **Spec direction.** The selected fix is to store a pointer selection snapshot, pass that snapshot through move and commit helpers, preserve same-ledger selection during refresh, and guard thread refresh against stale selection restore.\n\n---\n\n## C. Commit Section Added\n\n1. **Main repair commits.** The card now documents `bed5d24`, `e7ff7ff`, and `e1a55b5`, including what each commit covered and what each commit left uncovered.\n2. **Adjacent /**
````text
 * WHAT: Renders the active thread panel while preserving same-thread Codex control identity.
 * WHY: Thread note refreshes must not reset focused model and effort controls or their committed preferences.
 */
import { state, type ThreadCodexPreference } from '../../state.js';
import { renderTelemetry } from '../../telemetry/effect/render-telemetry.js';
import { renderVoiceStatus } from '../../voice/effect/render-voice-status.js';
import { renderVoiceDock } from '../../voice/effect/render-voice-dock.js';
import { renderThreadNotes } from './render-thread-notes.js';
import { applyThreadAccent } from './apply-thread-accent.js';
import { pinThreadFeedToLastMessage } from './pin-thread-feed-to-last-message.js';
import { renderThreadJumpButton, syncThreadJumpButtonVisibility } from './render-thread-jump-button.js';
import { restoreThreadDraft } from './persist-thread-draft.js';
import { restoreThreadScrollPosition, saveThreadScrollPosition } from './persist-thread-scroll.js';
import { resolveThreadTargetTitle } from '../helper/resolve-thread-target-title.js';
import { telemetry } from '../../telemetry/effect/telemetry.js';
import { codexEffortOptions, codexModelOptions } from '../../codex/helper/codex-run-options.js';
import { threadCodexCardId } from '../../codex/helper/thread-codex-card-id.js';

const defaultThreadCodexPreference: ThreadCodexPreference = { model: 'gpt-5.5', effort: 'xhigh' };

function threadCodexPreference(threadId: string): ThreadCodexPreference {
  // WHAT: Repair absent or invalid preference storage at its access boundary.
  // WHY: Restored runtime state may predate per-thread preferences.
  if (!state.threadCodexPreferencesByThreadId || typeof state.threadCodexPreferencesByThreadId !== 'object' || Array.isArray(state.threadCodexPreferencesByThreadId)) {
    state.threadCodexPreferencesByThreadId = {};
  }
  const preferences = state.threadCodexPreferencesByThreadId as Record<string, ThreadCodexPreference>;
  const existing = preferences[threadId];
  // WHAT: Reuse a complete preference object for the active thread.
  // WHY: Control remounts must preserve the operator's committed values.
  if (existing && typeof existing.model === 'string' && typeof existing.effort === 'string') return existing;
  const preference = { ...defaultThreadCodexPreference };
  preferences[threadId] = preference;
  return preference;
}

function renderThreadCodexSelect(input: { preference: 'model' | 'effort'; label: string; value: string; options: readonly string[]; onChange: (value: string) => void }): HTMLLabelElement {
  const field = document.createElement('label');
  field.className = 'thread-codex-field';
  const label = document.createElement('span');
  label.textContent = input.label;
  const select = document.createElement('select');
  select.className = 'thread-codex-select';
  select.dataset.codexPreference = input.preference;
  select.setAttribute('aria-label', `${input.label} for thread Codex`);
  for (const value of input.options) {
    const option = document.createElement('option');
    option.value = value;
    option.textContent = value;
    select.append(option);
  }
  select.value = input.value;
  select.addEventListener('change', () => input.onChange(select.value));
  field.replaceChildren(label, select);
  return field;
}

function renderThreadActions(threadId: string): void {
  const heading = document.querySelector('.thread-heading') as HTMLElement | null;
  // WHAT: Skip action rendering when the thread heading is absent.
  // WHY: Headless and partially mounted surfaces may render notes independently.
  if (!heading) return;
  let actions = heading.querySelector('.thread-actions') as HTMLElement | null;
  // WHAT: Create the stable actions host once for the thread panel.
  // WHY: Subsequent same-thread renders must retain descendant control identity.
  if (!actions) {
    actions = document.createElement('div');
    actions.className = 'thread-actions';
    heading.append(actions);
  }
  const preference = threadCodexPreference(threadId);
  const threadCodexModel = preference.model;
  const threadCodexEffort = preference.effort;
  // WHAT: Update button metadata in place for the same rendered thread.
  // WHY: Replacing controls would lose focus, listeners, and current select values.
  if (actions.dataset.threadId === threadId) {
    const button = actions.querySelector('.thread-codex-button') as HTMLButtonElement | null;
    // WHAT: Refresh the retained button's request operands when it exists.
    // WHY: Card ownership can change without requiring control remounting.
    if (button) {
      button.dataset.threadId = threadId;
      button.dataset.cardId = threadCodexCardId(state.activeLedger, threadId);
      button.dataset.codexModel = threadCodexModel;
      button.dataset.codexEffort = threadCodexEffort;
    }
    return;
  }
  actions.replaceChildren();
  actions.dataset.threadId = threadId;
  const cardId = threadCodexCardId(state.activeLedger, threadId);
  // WHAT: Leave actions empty when the thread has no owning card.
  // WHY: Codex requests require a card-scoped output target.
  if (!cardId) return;
  const button = document.createElement('button');
  button.className = 'thread-codex-button terminal-button terminal-button--compact';
  button.type = 'button';
  button.dataset.action = 'process-thread-codex';
  button.dataset.threadId = threadId;
  button.dataset.cardId = cardId;
  button.dataset.codexModel = threadCodexModel;
  button.dataset.codexEffort = threadCodexEffort;
  button.title = 'Start Codex from this thread';
  button.setAttribute('aria-label', button.title);
  const key = document.createElement('span');
  key.className = 'terminal-button__key';
  key.textContent = '>';
  const label = document.createElement('span');
  label.className = 'terminal-button__label';
  label.textContent = 'Codex';
  button.replaceChildren(key, label);
  const model = renderThreadCodexSelect({
    preference: 'model',
    label: 'Model',
    value: threadCodexModel,
    options: codexModelOptions,
    onChange: (value) => {
      preference.model = value;
      button.dataset.codexModel = value;
    },
  });
  const effort = renderThreadCodexSelect({
    preference: 'effort',
    label: 'Effort',
    value: threadCodexEffort,
    options: codexEffortOptions,
    onChange: (value) => {
      preference.effort = value;
      button.dataset.codexEffort = value;
    },
  });
  actions.append(model, effort, button);
}

export function renderThreadPanel(): void {
  const panel = document.querySelector('.thread-panel') as HTMLElement;
  const inspector = document.querySelector('.panel') as HTMLElement;
  const shell = document.querySelector('.shell') as HTMLElement;
  const shouldOpenThread = Boolean(state.threadPanelOpen || state.activeTool === 'thread');
  const activeThreadId = String(state.threadId ?? '');
  const shouldPinThread = Boolean(shouldOpenThread && state.threadPinOnRender);
  if (shouldOpenThread && !shouldPinThread && activeThreadId && state.renderedThreadId === activeThreadId) {
    saveThreadScrollPosition(activeThreadId);
  }
  inspector.hidden = false;
  panel.hidden = !shouldOpenThread;
  shell.classList.toggle('has-inspector', shouldOpenThread);
  const target = document.querySelector('.thread-target') as HTMLElement;
  target.replaceChildren();
  if (state.threadId) {
    const title = document.createElement('span');
    title.className = 'thread-target-title';
    title.textContent = resolveThreadTargetTitle(state.threadId);
    const id = document.createElement('span');
    id.className = 'thread-target-id';
    id.textContent = `Open: ${state.threadId}`;
    target.append(title, id);
  } else {
    target.textContent = 'No thread selected';
  }
  renderThreadActions(activeThreadId);
  applyThreadAccent();
  telemetry('render-thread-panel', { threadId: state.threadId });
  renderThreadNotes();
  renderThreadJumpButton();
  state.renderedThreadId = activeThreadId;
  renderVoiceDock();
  restoreThreadDraft();
  renderVoiceStatus();
  renderTelemetry();
  if (shouldPinThread) {
    state.threadPinOnRender = false;
    pinThreadFeedToLastMessage();
  } else if (shouldOpenThread) {
    restoreThreadScrollPosition(activeThreadId);
  }
  syncThreadJumpButtonVisibility();
}
````

````text
/**
 * WHAT: Renders the active thread notes from the current ledger into the inspector.
 * WHY: Voice and text notes must appear as conversation ledger entries, not only draft text.
 */
import { state } from '../../state.js';
import { renderLedgerCardMarkdown } from '../../ledger/component/render-ledger-card-markdown.js';
import { sendActiveLedgerMutation } from '../../ledger/effect/send-active-ledger-mutation.js';
import { deletedNoteIdSet } from '../../ledger/helper/normalize-deleted-note-ids.js';
import { expireStaleVoiceTranscription, scheduleVoiceTranscriptionTimeout } from '../../voice/helper/expire-stale-voice-transcription.js';

type ThreadImageSizes = Record<string, { width?: number; height?: number }>;

const pendingThreadImageSizeTimers = new Map<string, ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>();

function hashText(value: string): string {
  let hash = 2166136261;
  for (let index = 0; index < value.length; index += 1) {
    hash ^= value.charCodeAt(index);
    hash = Math.imul(hash, 16777619);
  }
  return (hash >>> 0).toString(36);
}

function noteText(note: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  return String(note.message ?? note.body ?? '');
}

function normalizeCodexKind(note: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  return String(note.codexKind ?? '').replace(/[^a-z0-9_-]+/gi, '-').toLowerCase();
}

function imageSizeSignature(note: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  const sizes = threadImageSizes(note.imageSizes);
  const entries = Object.entries(sizes).sort(([left], [right]) => left.localeCompare(right));
  return entries.map(([source, dimensions]) => `${source}:${dimensions.width ?? ''}x${dimensions.height ?? ''}`).join(',');
}

function threadNotesSignature(threadId: string, notes: Array<Record<string, unknown>>): string {
  const parts = [threadId, String(notes.length)];
  for (const note of notes) {
    const text = noteText(note);
    parts.push([
      String(note.id ?? ''),
      String(note.role ?? 'operator'),
      String(note.status ?? ''),
      String(note.voiceFileRef ?? ''),
      String(note.transcriptionStartedAt ?? ''),
      String(note.optimistic ?? ''),
      codexNoteClass(note),
      String(note.codexTool ?? ''),
      String(note.codexExitCode ?? ''),
      imageSizeSignature(note),
      String(text.length),
      hashText(text)
    ].join(':'));
  }
  return hashText(parts.join('|'));
}

function noteListDataset(list: HTMLElement): DOMStringMap {
  const element = list as HTMLElement & { dataset?: DOMStringMap };
  if (!element.dataset) element.dataset = {} as DOMStringMap;
  return element.dataset;
}

function codexNoteClass(note: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  const kind = normalizeCodexKind(note);
  return kind ? `is-codex-run-event is-codex-${kind}` : '';
}

function isCodexToolCallNote(note: Record<string, unknown>): boolean {
  return normalizeCodexKind(note) === 'tool_call';
}

function stripOuterQuotes(value: string): string {
  const trimmed = value.trim();
  const quote = trimmed[0];
  if ((quote === '"' || quote === "'") && trimmed.endsWith(quote)) return trimmed.slice(1, -1).trim();
  return trimmed;
}

function stripShellWrapper(command: string): string {
  const normalized = command.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
  const shell = normalized.match(/^(?:\/usr\/bin\/env\s+)?(?:\/[^\s]+\/)?(?:zsh|bash|sh)\s+-lc\s+(.+)$/);
  return shell?.[1] ? stripOuterQuotes(shell[1]) : normalized;
}

function commandFromToolCallMessage(message: string): string {
  return message.match(/\*\*Tool call\*\*\s+`([^`]+)`/)?.[1]?.trim() ?? '';
}

function codexToolCommand(note: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  return stripShellWrapper(String(note.codexTool ?? '').trim() || commandFromToolCallMessage(noteText(note)) || 'command');
}

function commandHasToken(command: string, tokens: string[]): boolean {
  const escaped = tokens.map((token) => token.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&')).join('|');
  return new RegExp(`(^|[\\s;&|()])(?:${escaped})(?=\\s|$)`, 'i').test(command);
}

function codexToolAction(command: string): string {
  if (commandHasToken(command, ['git', 'gh'])) return 'Git';
  if (commandHasToken(command, ['rg', 'grep', 'find', 'fd'])) return 'Search';
  if (commandHasToken(command, ['apply_patch', 'tee', 'touch', 'mkdir', 'rm', 'mv', 'cp', 'chmod', 'chown'])) return 'Write';
  if (/(^|[\s;&|()])(?:cat|sed|nl|head|tail|less|wc)(?=\s|$)/i.test(command)) return 'Read';
  if (/(^|[\s;&|()])(?:npm|pnpm|yarn|node|tsx|tsc|vitest|jest|playwright|pytest)(?=\s|$)/i.test(command)) return 'Ran';
  return 'Ran';
}

function shortenText(value: string, maxLength: number): string {
  const compact = value.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
  if (compact.length <= maxLength) return compact;
  const headLength = Math.max(24, Math.floor(maxLength * 0.62));
  const tailLength = Math.max(12, maxLength - headLength - 5);
  return `${compact.slice(0, headLength).trimEnd()} ... ${compact.slice(-tailLength).trimStart()}`;
}

function codexToolStatus(note: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  const status = String(note.status ?? '').trim();
  const exitCode = String(note.codexExitCode ?? '').trim();
  if (status && exitCode) return `${status} / code ${exitCode}`;
  if (status) return status;
  if (exitCode) return `code ${exitCode}`;
  return '';
}

function renderCodexToolCallNote(note: Record<string, unknown>, body: HTMLElement): HTMLElement {
  const command = codexToolCommand(note);
  const action = codexToolAction(command);
  const details = document.createElement('details');
  details.className = 'codex-tool-call';
  details.dataset.codexToolAction = action.toLowerCase();

  const summary = document.createElement('summary');
  summary.className = 'codex-tool-call-summary';
  summary.title = command;

  const actionLabel = document.createElement('span');
  actionLabel.className = 'codex-tool-call-action';
  actionLabel.textContent = action;

  const commandLabel = document.createElement('span');
  commandLabel.className = 'codex-tool-call-command';
  commandLabel.textContent = shortenText(command, 118);

  const status = codexToolStatus(note);
  const statusLabel = document.createElement('span');
  statusLabel.className = 'codex-tool-call-status';
  statusLabel.textContent = status;
  statusLabel.setAttribute('aria-hidden', status ? 'false' : 'true');

  summary.append(actionLabel, commandLabel, statusLabel);
  body.classList.add('codex-tool-call-details');
  details.append(summary, body);
  return details;
}

function threadImageSizes(value: unknown): ThreadImageSizes {
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return {};
  const sizes: ThreadImageSizes = {};
  for (const [source, dimensions] of Object.entries(value as Record<string, unknown>)) {
    if (!dimensions || typeof dimensions !== 'object' || Array.isArray(dimensions)) continue;
    const width = Number((dimensions as Record<string, unknown>).width);
    const height = Number((dimensions as Record<string, unknown>).height);
    sizes[source] = {
      width: Number.isFinite(width) && width > 0 ? width : undefined,
      height: Number.isFinite(height) && height > 0 ? height : undefined
    };
  }
  return sizes;
}

function persistThreadImageSize(input: { threadId: string; note: Record<string, unknown>; source: string; width: number; height: number }): void {
  const noteId = String(input.note.id ?? '');
  if (!input.threadId || !noteId) return;
  const imageSizes = threadImageSizes(input.note.imageSizes);
  const existing = imageSizes[input.source] ?? {};
  if (existing.width === input.width && existing.height === input.height) return;
  imageSizes[input.source] = { width: input.width, height: input.height };
  input.note.imageSizes = imageSizes;
  const timerKey = `${input.threadId}:${noteId}:${input.source}`;
  const pending = pendingThreadImageSizeTimers.get(timerKey);
  if (pending) clearTimeout(pending);
  pendingThreadImageSizeTimers.set(timerKey, setTimeout(() => {
    pendingThreadImageSizeTimers.delete(timerKey);
    void sendActiveLedgerMutation({
      action: 'update-note',
      note: { id: noteId, threadId: input.threadId, imageSizes: threadImageSizes(input.note.imageSizes) }
    });
  }, 240));
}

export function renderThreadNotes(): void {
  const existing = document.querySelector('.thread-note-list') as HTMLElement | null;
  const feed = document.querySelector('.thread-feed') as HTMLElement | null;
  if (!feed && !existing) return;
  const list = existing ?? document.createElement('ol');
  list.className = 'thread-note-list';
  if (!existing) feed?.append(list);
  const deletedIds = state.threadId && state.activeLedger ? deletedNoteIdSet(state.activeLedger, state.threadId) : new Set<string>();
  const notes = state.threadId ? (state.activeLedger?.notes?.[state.threadId] ?? []).filter((note: Record<string, unknown>) => !deletedIds.has(String(note.id ?? ''))) : [];
  for (const note of notes) {
    if (!expireStaleVoiceTranscription(note)) scheduleVoiceTranscriptionTimeout({ threadId: state.threadId, note });
  }
  const signature = threadNotesSignature(String(state.threadId ?? ''), notes);
  const dataset = noteListDataset(list);
  if (existing && dataset.threadId === String(state.threadId ?? '') && dataset.notesSignature === signature) return;
  dataset.threadId = String(state.threadId ?? '');
  dataset.notesSignature = signature;
  list.replaceChildren();
  for (const note of notes) {
    const status = String(note.status ?? '');
    const role = String(note.role ?? 'operator').toLowerCase();
    const agentOwned = role === 'agent' || role === 'assistant';
    const noteId = String(note.id ?? '');
    const normalizedStatus = status.toLowerCase();
    const busy = /committing|uploading|transcribing|retrying/.test(normalizedStatus);
    const retryable = Boolean(note.voiceFileRef) && /failed|not configured|unavailable/.test(normalizedStatus);
    const item = document.createElement('li');
    item.className = ['thread-note', note.voiceFileRef ? 'voice-note' : '', note.optimistic ? 'is-optimistic' : '', busy ? 'is-busy' : '', retryable ? 'is-retryable' : '', codexNoteClass(note), agentOwned ? 'is-agent' : 'is-operator'].filter(Boolean).join(' ');
    const body = renderLedgerCardMarkdown(noteText(note), {
      imageSizes: threadImageSizes(note.imageSizes),
      mediaSurface: 'thread',
      onImageResize: (source, dimensions) => {
        persistThreadImageSize({
          threadId: state.threadId,
          note,
          source,
          width: dimensions.width,
          height: dimensions.height
        });
      }
    });
    body.classList.add('thread-note-message');
    const noteBody = isCodexToolCallNote(note) ? renderCodexToolCallNote(note, body) : body;
    const meta = document.createElement('span');
    meta.className = 'thread-note-meta';
    meta.textContent = status;
    const deleteButton = document.createElement('button');
    deleteButton.className = 'thread-note-delete terminal-button terminal-button--compact';
    deleteButton.type = 'button';
    deleteButton.dataset.action = 'confirm-delete-note';
    deleteButton.dataset.threadId = state.threadId;
    deleteButton.dataset.noteId = noteId;
    deleteButton.title = 'Delete note';
    deleteButton.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Delete note');
    deleteButton.textContent = 'X';
    item.append(noteBody);
    if (status && !busy) item.append(meta);
    if (noteId) item.append(deleteButton);
    if (busy) {
      const spinner = document.createElement('span');
      spinner.className = 'thread-note-spinner';
      spinner.textContent = normalizedStatus || 'processing';
      item.append(spinner);
    }
    if (retryable) {
      const retry = document.createElement('button');
      retry.className = 'thread-note-retry terminal-button terminal-button--compact';
      retry.type = 'button';
      retry.dataset.action = 'voice-retry';
      retry.dataset.threadId = state.threadId;
      retry.dataset.noteId = String(note.id ?? '');
      retry.dataset.voiceFileRef = String(note.voiceFileRef ?? '');
      retry.textContent = 'Retry';
      item.append(retry);
    }
    list.append(item);
  }
}
````

````text
export type SelectionState = { cardIds: string[]; zoneIds: string[]; groupIds: string[] };

export type PointerSelectionSnapshot = SelectionState & {
  targetKind: string;
  targetId: string;
  ledgerStateId: string;
};

export type LedgerReconciliationState = {
  routeEpoch: number;
  routeLedgerStateId: string;
  nextRequestSequence: number;
  lastAppliedServerRevision: number;
  lastAppliedSequence: number;
  localGeometryRevisions: Record<string, number>;
  failedLoadCount: number;
  lastFailedLoad: null | {
    at: string;
    ledgerStateId: string;
    routeEpoch: number;
    sequence: number;
    source: string;
    reason: string;
  };
};

export type ThreadContentRefreshScope = {
  ledgerId: string;
  threadId: string;
  contentFile: string;
};

export type LedgerContentRefreshState = {
  inFlight: boolean;
  ledgerReasons: string[];
  changedContentFiles: string[];
  threadReasons: string[];
  threadScope: ThreadContentRefreshScope | null;
};

export type ThreadCodexPreference = {
  model: string;
  effort: string;
};

export const state: any = {
  routePath: globalThis.window?.location?.pathname ?? '/',
````

````text
.thread-panel {

}

}

.thread-heading .kicker {

.thread-jump-bottom-frame {
  position: absolute;
  right: 18px;
  bottom: 16px;
  z-index: 18;
  display: flex;
  justify-content: flex-end;
  pointer-events: none;
}

.thread-jump-bottom {
  --terminal-button-background: linear-gradient(165deg, #18222d 0%, #121920 54%, #0c1117 100%);
  --terminal-button-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--thread-accent), white 58%);
  --terminal-button-gradient-shadow: linear-gradient(90deg, color-mix(in srgb, var(--thread-accent), transparent 24%), rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.16));
  position: relative;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  width: 34px;
  min-width: 34px;
  height: 34px;
  min-height: 34px;
  margin-right: 2px;
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 3px;
  background: var(--terminal-button-background);
  color: var(--terminal-button-color);
  box-shadow:
    inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--thread-accent), transparent 48%),
    inset 0 0 14px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.09),
    0 12px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.52);
  opacity: 0.92;
  pointer-events: auto;
  transform: translateY(0);
  transition:
    opacity 120ms ease,
    transform 120ms ease,
    box-shadow 120ms ease,
    color 120ms ease,
    filter 120ms ease;
}

.thread-jump-bottom[hidden] {
  display: none;
}

.thread-jump-bottom::after {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  inset: -8px;
  z-index: -1;
  border-radius: 16px;
  background: var(--terminal-button-gradient-shadow);
  filter: blur(10px);
  opacity: 0;
  transition: opacity 140ms ease;
}

.thread-jump-bottom:hover {
  color: #f3f6fb;
  filter: brightness(1.16) saturate(1.08);
  transform: translateY(-1px);
  box-shadow:
    inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--thread-accent), white 16%),
    inset 0 0 16px color-mix(in srgb, var(--thread-accent), transparent 72%),
    0 14px 28px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.58);
}

.thread-jump-bottom:hover::after {
  opacity: 0.34;
}

.thread-jump-bottom:focus-visible {
  color: #f3f6fb;
  outline: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--thread-accent), white 28%);
  outline-offset: 3px;
  box-shadow:
    inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--thread-accent), white 22%),
    0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--thread-accent), transparent 70%),
    0 14px 28px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.58);
}

.thread-jump-bottom-chevron {
  position: relative;
  display: block;
  width: 12px;
  height: 12px;
}

.thread-jump-bottom-chevron::before {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  top: 1px;
  left: 2px;
  width: 8px;
  height: 8px;
  border-right: 2px solid currentColor;
  border-bottom: 2px solid currentColor;
  transform: rotate(45deg);
}

.thread-note {
  position: relative;
  display: grid;
  gap: 6px;
  min-width: 0;
  max-width: min(86%, 520px);
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
  background: transparent;
````

````text
import { state } from '../../state.js';

function threadScrollState(): Record<string, number> {
  if (!state.threadScrollTopByThreadId || typeof state.threadScrollTopByThreadId !== 'object') {
    state.threadScrollTopByThreadId = {};
  }
  return state.threadScrollTopByThreadId;
}

function threadScrollElement(): HTMLElement | null {
  if (typeof document === 'undefined') return null;
  return document.querySelector('.thread-panel .chat') as HTMLElement | null;
}

export function hasSavedThreadScrollPosition(threadId = String(state.threadId ?? '')): boolean {
  if (!threadId) return false;
  return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(threadScrollState(), threadId);
}

export function saveThreadScrollPosition(threadId = String(state.threadId ?? '')): void {
  if (!threadId) return;
  const chat = threadScrollElement();
  if (!chat) return;
  const scrollTop = Number(chat.scrollTop);
  if (!Number.isFinite(scrollTop)) return;
  threadScrollState()[threadId] = Math.max(0, scrollTop);
}

export function restoreThreadScrollPosition(threadId = String(state.threadId ?? '')): boolean {
  if (!hasSavedThreadScrollPosition(threadId)) return false;
  const chat = threadScrollElement();
  if (!chat) return false;
  const savedScrollTop = threadScrollState()[threadId];
  const restore = () => {
    const maxScrollTop = Math.max(0, Number(chat.scrollHeight ?? 0) - Number(chat.clientHeight ?? 0));
    chat.scrollTop = Math.min(savedScrollTop, maxScrollTop || savedScrollTop);
  };
  restore();
  globalThis.requestAnimationFrame?.(() => restore());
  return true;
}
````

````text
/**
 * WHAT: Pins the thread conversation viewport to the newest rendered note.
 * WHY: Opening a card thread should land on the latest operator/agent exchange.
 */
import { syncThreadJumpButtonVisibility } from './render-thread-jump-button.js';

export function pinThreadFeedToLastMessage(options: { behavior?: ScrollBehavior } = {}): void {
  const chat = document.querySelector('.thread-panel .chat') as HTMLElement | null;
  const list = document.querySelector('.thread-note-list') as HTMLElement | null;
  if (!chat) return;
  const scrollOptions: ScrollIntoViewOptions = options.behavior === 'smooth'
    ? { block: 'end', inline: 'nearest', behavior: options.behavior }
    : { block: 'end', inline: 'nearest' };
  const pin = () => {
    const lastNote = list?.lastElementChild as HTMLElement | null;
    lastNote?.scrollIntoView?.(scrollOptions);
    if (options.behavior === 'smooth' && typeof chat.scrollTo === 'function') {
      chat.scrollTo({ top: chat.scrollHeight, behavior: options.behavior });
    } else {
      chat.scrollTop = chat.scrollHeight;
    }
    syncThreadJumpButtonVisibility();
  };
  pin();
  globalThis.requestAnimationFrame?.(() => pin());
}
````

````text
/**
 * WHAT: Renders and updates the thread feed jump-to-bottom control.
 * WHY: Long threads need a quick return path to the newest note without moving the composer.
 */
const threadJumpScrollHandlers = new WeakMap<HTMLElement, EventListener>();

function threadChatElement(): HTMLElement | null {
  if (typeof document === 'undefined') return null;
  return document.querySelector('.thread-panel .chat') as HTMLElement | null;
}

function threadJumpFrameHost(chat = threadChatElement()): HTMLElement | null {
  if (typeof document === 'undefined') return null;
  return (document.querySelector('.thread-panel .thread-chat-shell') as HTMLElement | null) ?? chat;
}

function threadJumpFrame(): HTMLElement | null {
  if (typeof document === 'undefined') return null;
  return document.querySelector('.thread-panel .thread-jump-bottom-frame') as HTMLElement | null;
}

function threadJumpButton(): HTMLButtonElement | null {
  if (typeof document === 'undefined') return null;
  return document.querySelector('.thread-panel .thread-jump-bottom') as HTMLButtonElement | null;
}

export function syncThreadJumpButtonVisibility(): void {
  const chat = threadChatElement();
  const button = threadJumpButton();
  if (!chat || !button) return;
  const scrollTop = Math.max(0, Number(chat.scrollTop ?? 0));
  const scrollHeight = Math.max(0, Number(chat.scrollHeight ?? 0));
  const clientHeight = Math.max(0, Number(chat.clientHeight ?? 0));
  const maxScrollTop = Math.max(0, scrollHeight - clientHeight);
  const bottomDistance = Math.max(0, maxScrollTop - scrollTop);
  const shouldShow = maxScrollTop > 8 && bottomDistance > 72;
  button.hidden = !shouldShow;
  button.setAttribute('aria-hidden', shouldShow ? 'false' : 'true');
}

export function renderThreadJumpButton(): void {
  const chat = threadChatElement();
  const host = threadJumpFrameHost(chat);
  if (!chat || !host) return;
  let frame = threadJumpFrame();
  let button = threadJumpButton();
  if (!frame) {
    frame = document.createElement('div');
    frame.className = 'thread-jump-bottom-frame';
  }
  if (frame.parentElement !== host) {
    host.append(frame);
  }
  if (!button) {
    button = document.createElement('button');
    button.className = 'thread-jump-bottom';
    button.type = 'button';
    button.dataset.action = 'jump-thread-bottom';
    button.title = 'Jump to bottom';
    button.setAttribute('aria-label', button.title);
    const chevron = document.createElement('span');
    chevron.className = 'thread-jump-bottom-chevron';
    chevron.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
    button.replaceChildren(chevron);
  }
  if (button.parentElement !== frame) {
    frame.append(button);
  }
  if (!threadJumpScrollHandlers.has(chat)) {
    const sync = () => syncThreadJumpButtonVisibility();
    chat.addEventListener('scroll', sync, { passive: true });
    threadJumpScrollHandlers.set(chat, sync);
  }
  syncThreadJumpButtonVisibility();
  globalThis.requestAnimationFrame?.(() => syncThreadJumpButtonVisibility());
}
````
